title: Fair isle baby blanket
subtitle: A 75 by 90 cm cot blanket in a two-colour stranded Fair Isle border and plain centre.
excerpt: A 75 by 90 cm cot blanket in DK worked flat, with a ten-row Fair Isle border at cast-on and cast-off and a stocking-stitch centre. The stranded border uses a simple eight-stitch geometric repeat in two colours. About 230 g of the main colour and 50 g of the contrast.
sourceNotes: Fair Isle stranded colourwork with geometric repeats is documented in Weldon's Practical Knitter, 12th series (1896), §Stranded Knitting Borders, as a Shetland Islands technique for decorative edgings on nursery items. The specific eight-stitch X-and-O repeat appears in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), §Fair Isle Patterns.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 30 rows = 10 × 10 cm in stocking stitch on 4 mm needles, blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: A two-colour stranded colourwork technique where both yarn colours are carried across every row. The colour not being knitted is stranded (floated) across the wrong side of the work. Floats should not exceed 3 to 5 stitches in length to prevent puckering. Fair Isle traditionally uses geometric repeats with no float longer than about 5 stitches.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat on 4 mm needles. A ten-row two-colour
Fair Isle
border sits at cast-on and cast-off. The centre is stocking stitch. Finished size: 75 cm wide by 90 cm long.

Single-panel construction; no seaming. The stranded border uses a simple eight-stitch X-and-O geometric repeat in the main colour and one contrast colour. The border rows require managing two yarns simultaneously; the stocking-stitch centre is single-colour throughout. The contrast yarn is cut at the end of each border, so mid-project yarn management is minimal. Budget about 230 g of the main colour (about 505 m / 552 yards) and 50 g of the contrast colour (about 110 m / 120 yards). The blanket needs wet blocking to prevent the stocking-stitch centre from curling.
What you need

items.name: Main colour (MC)
items.qty: 230 g (about 505 m / 552 yards) of DK-weight machine-washable yarn

items.name: Contrast colour (CC)
items.qty: 50 g (about 110 m / 120 yards) of DK-weight yarn in a contrasting colour

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) circular needle, 80 cm or longer

items.name: Blocking mat and pins
items.qty: Recommended, stocking-stitch centre curls without blocking

content.text: Gauge

22 stitches and 30 rows to 10 cm in stocking stitch on 4 mm needles, blocked. Stranded rows tend to pull in by 1 to 2 stitches per 10 cm compared to single-colour rows; the border has a slightly denser appearance which is expected.
Stitches used
Pattern
Cast-on
Using MC and the long-tail cast-on, cast on 165 stitches (a multiple of 8 + 5 edge stitches). Long-tail tail: (4 × 165) / 10 + 15 = 66 + 15 = 81 cm. Measure 95 cm.
Bottom border (10 rows Fair Isle)
Rows 1, 2 (MC only): k all RS, p all WS.

Rows 3, 8 (Fair Isle border, 8-stitch X-and-O repeat): RS rows: *2MC, 2CC, 2MC, 2CC; repeat from * to last 5 sts, 5MC. WS rows: purl working the colour sequence in reverse. Carry the unused colour across the wrong side, catching every 3rd stitch if a float exceeds 5 stitches.
Rows 9, 10 (MC only): k all RS, p all WS. Cut CC. Border is complete.
Centre (stocking stitch)
Using MC only, work stocking stitch (k RS, p WS) until the blanket measures 80 cm from the cast-on edge.
Top border
Join CC. Work 10 rows Fair Isle border identical to the bottom border. Total blanket length: 90 cm.
Stitch count check-ins
At row 135 (about 45 cm): count across. You should have 165 stitches. At row 268 (about 89.5 cm): count again before casting off.
Common faults

Border pulling in relative to the stocking-stitch centre: stranded rows were knitted too tightly. When working Fair Isle rows, spread the stitches across the right needle before knitting each stitch so floats lie loose.

Pattern misaligned between RS rows: the border sequence was not read correctly on a WS row. Note that WS Fair Isle rows are purled and the colour sequence runs in reverse (right to left instead of left to right).
Cast-off
Cast off knitwise with MC after the final garter row of the top border, with a relaxed tension.
Finishing
Weave in all CC tails on the wrong side. Wet block the finished blanket to prevent curling of the stocking-stitch centre and to open the Fair Isle borders.
Care
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle for superwash DK. Lay flat to dry, reshaping to measurements.
What to try next

From a border-only Fair Isle blanket, the next step is an all-over stranded blanket: the same X-and-O repeat across the full width and length, with both colours active throughout. This requires managing the float tension consistently for the entire project.
